title: A look at EBean and lightweight alternatives

videos.script: Lessons ten and eleven gave the bookshop an ORM. Books became objects, and most of the SQL disappeared. {{jpa}} Then the bill arrived. One select per book in the listing. An exception when an author was read too late. {{bill}} JPA is not the only way from Java to a database. Between it and plain JDBC sits a whole row of libraries. {{row}} Each one keeps a different part of what JPA gives you, and drops a different part of what it costs. {{trade}} EBean is an ORM with no session to outlive. jOOQ writes SQL as Java, and the compiler checks it against the schema. {{ebean-jooq}} MyBatis keeps the SQL as text, in mappers. JDBI is JDBC with the ceremony taken out. {{mybatis-jdbi}} You will read all of them through one question. Who writes the SQL, and when do you find out it is wrong? {{question}} Then you run JDBI against the bookshop's own database. You break a column name on purpose, and watch when the mistake shows up. {{run}} After this lesson, you can open any of these in somebody's codebase and say what the team bought with it.
